cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel, has finished praying at the new temple, and the people have gone home joyful (2 Chronicles 7:1, 10). Now the house of the LORD and his royal palace are DONE, with everything he set his heart on doing for them carried out. That man finished his WHOLE to-do list, friend, and I've had "organize the sprinkles" on mine since the day I got here.

cards.question: One night, the LORD appears to Solomon. What's the first thing He tells him?
The LORD tells Solomon He has chosen this place for Himself as a house of ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about hard days. What if He closes the sky so there's no rain, or commands the locusts to eat up the land, or sends a plague among His people?

cards.question: If the LORD stops the rain, sends locusts or sends a plague, He says He will hear from heaven if His people do something. What is it?

answers.text: Offer more sacrifices at the temple
Call on their king for help

cards.text: They also need to pray and turn from their wicked ways. That's turning AROUND, like realizing you've been driving the wrong way for an hour and actually taking the exit.

cards.question: The LORD says that when His people turn back to Him, He will hear from heaven, forgive their sin and ___ their land.

cards.text: And this brand-new temple? The LORD says from now on His eyes will be open and His ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.

cards.question: The LORD tells Solomon that His eyes and His heart will be at this temple for all time.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to Solomon himself: if you walk before Me as your father David walked, doing all I've commanded and keeping My statutes and ordinances. Following in the footsteps of DAVID? I bet that's a LOT to live up to.

cards.question: If Solomon walks before the LORD as his father David walked, the LORD says He will establish Solomon's royal ___.

cards.text: It's the same covenant the LORD made with David when He said, "You will never fail to have a man to rule over Israel."

cards.question: Then the LORD gives the other side and warns about turning away from His statutes and commandments. What else does He warn about going off to do?

answers.text: Build altars on the high hills

cards.question: If Israel goes off to serve other gods, what does the LORD say He will do to them?

cards.text: And the temple He set apart for His Name? He'll banish it from His presence and make it an object of scorn and ridicule among all the peoples.

cards.question: The LORD says that when this temple has become a heap of rubble, the people passing by will pay it no attention.

cards.text: All who pass by will be appalled and ask, "Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?"

Others will answer that they forsook the LORD, the God of their fathers who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and embraced other gods, so He brought all this disaster on them. That's a heavy word, friend, and Solomon heard every bit of it.
